newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Weather delays Ariane rocket launch.
newsitem.headline: Weather delays Ariane rocket launch.

text.p: Strong winds high above French Guiana have delayed Thursday's scheduled launch of Western Europe's 94th Ariane rocket carrying a satellite for INTELSAT.

Officials of the French Space Agency (CNES) said wind velocity at an altitude of 10 km to 20 km (seven to 14 miles) was higher than permitted for a safe launch. They said a launch might be attempted on Friday.
The Ariane-4 rocket was scheduled to launch INTELSAT 801, the first in a new series of satellites for the Washington-based International Telecommunications Satellite Organisation (INTELSAT).
Ariane rockets are launched from the European Space Agency (ESA) centre in Kourou, French Guiana on the northeast coast of South America.
